title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck's notes on the 'structure at infinity' of the moduli stacks M_{g,ν}. X is a compactified stratified space (the stable-curve compactification as a stratified topos), Θ is the divisor at infinity, and 'parties admissibles' are closed unions of strata. For admissible Σ' ⊂ Σ'', V_{Σ',Σ''} denotes a tubular-neighbourhood topos (a germ of neighbourhood, or homotopy neighbourhood) of Σ' in Σ''. V*_{Σ',X} is the deleted neighbourhood, i.e. the neighbourhood intersected with the open part X∖Θ. The previous page (256) records that the trace of an admissible Σ_1 on such a neighbourhood is again of the same type: V_{Σ',Σ''} ∩ Σ_1 = V_{Σ'∩Σ_1, Σ''∩Σ_1}.

On this page he introduces a three-index family (257): V^Σ_{Σ',Σ''} := V_{Σ',Σ''} ∖ (V_{Σ',Σ''} ∩ Σ). This is the neighbourhood of Σ' in Σ'' with the admissible part Σ removed. Special cases:
(i) Σ' = Σ''. Then V_{Σ',Σ'} = Σ', so one gets Σ'∖Σ, which is Σ' itself if Σ = ∅.
(ii) Σ'' = X and Σ = Θ. One gets V*_{Σ',X}, the 'deleted tubular neighbourhood' of a boundary stratum inside the open moduli space. Its π_1 is what the previous pages want to express through the local groups π_{Δr} and \tilde π_{Δr}.

He then adds a further admissible Σ'_0 ⊂ Σ' and forms (258): V^{Σ∖Σ∩Σ'_0}_{Σ'∖Σ'_0, Σ''∖Σ'_0}. This is the same construction carried out inside the open complement of Σ'_0. He warns not to confuse it with V^{Σ∪Σ'_0}_{Σ',Σ''}.

Example: Σ = ∅ and Σ'_0 ⊂ Σ' ⊂ Σ'' = X. Then V^{Σ'_0}_{Σ',X} differs from V_{Σ'∖Σ'_0, X∖Σ'_0}. If Σ'_0 = Σ':
- the first is V^{Σ'}_{Σ',X}, the deleted neighbourhood of Σ'. For Σ' = Θ a smooth divisor this is V*_{Θ,X}, homotopy equivalent to a punctured-disc bundle over Θ.
- the second is the empty topos.

The next page shows that type (258) reduces to type (257) by passing to the complement X∖Σ'_0. The general Σ'' reduces to Σ'' = X once one knows how to pass from X to Σ''. Both reductions are needed in the 'Dedekind system' formalism. Purpose: to obtain a closed family of 'relative links' whose fundamental groups (groupoids) can all be described combinatorially from the local data π_{Δr}, \tilde π_{Δr}. This is the missing structure needed to describe the profinite/discrete fundamental groupoids at infinity of M_{g,ν}.
errors: Notational slip: in the 'ne pas confondre' line and in the example he writes Σ_0 where Σ'_0 is meant (V^{Σ∪Σ_0}, V^{Σ_0}_{Σ',X}, V_{Σ'∖Σ_0, X∖Σ_0}).

In (257) the subtracted term is written V_{Σ',Σ''}∩Σ. By (256) it equals V_{Σ'∩Σ, Σ''∩Σ}, so the definition is consistent. Strictly, intersecting a neighbourhood germ with a closed part requires the neighbourhood formalism to be compatible with restriction, which is (256). No genuine error.
'Fibré en disques épointés' holds only up to homotopy / for a sufficiently small tubular neighbourhood. He corrects 'est' to 'équivalent', acknowledging this.

ideas.what: Three-index family V^Σ_{Σ',Σ''} of neighbourhood topoi of a stratum-union Σ' in Σ'', minus another admissible part Σ, closed under the natural operations (trace, complement).
ideas.modern_name: Homotopy links / relative tubular neighbourhoods in stratified spaces; exit-path and link data of a stratified space
ideas.usually_credited_to: Quinn (homotopy links, 1988); Mather/Thom tubular data; later Treumann, Lurie (exit paths, stratified ∞-categories)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme alludes to the 'structure at infinity' of the Teichmüller tower and to tubular neighbourhoods at infinity, but not to this formalism

ideas.what: The deleted tubular neighbourhood of the boundary divisor of M̄_{g,ν} is a punctured-disc bundle over Θ, whose π_1 gives the local monodromy/inertia at infinity.
ideas.modern_name: Deleted tubular neighbourhood; punctured-disc bundle; boundary/inertia groups at infinity
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard (Deligne–Mumford compactification, Harer, Ivanov; Nakamura and others in the profinite setting)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse (general discussion of tangential base points and divisors at infinity)

ideas.what: Reduction of neighbourhood topoi relative to Σ'_0 to the absolute case by passing to the open complement of an admissible part.
ideas.modern_name: Restriction of stratified data to open unions of strata

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up a systematic indexed family of relative neighbourhood (link) topoi V^Σ_{Σ',Σ''} for the stratification at infinity of M̄_{g,ν}. He intends to express all their fundamental groupoids in terms of the local groups π_{Δr}, \tilde π_{Δr}, i.e. a combinatorial 'Dedekind system' presentation of the fundamental groupoid at infinity. The program is announced but not carried out here.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This anticipates descriptions of the profinite fundamental groupoids at infinity of moduli of curves via strata and their links. Such descriptions appear in pieces in the literature (Nakamura, Boggi, Hoshi–Mochizuki on boundary groups), but not in this general indexed-neighbourhood formalism. Of modest interest, since stratified homotopy theory now covers it abstractly.

deep.surprise_reason: Careful but essentially routine bookkeeping of neighbourhood/link topoi in a stratified space. The concept itself (homotopy links, exit-path data) is standard today. The interest is mainly historical, as part of Grothendieck's unpublished program on the structure at infinity of M_{g,ν}.
transcription_corrections: '{+i.e. on a Σ'_0⊂Σ'⊂X+}' is written as 'ici on a Σ'_0 ⊂ Σ' ⊂ X' between the lines.
In the 'ne pas confondre' formulas the manuscript indeed has Σ_0 (unprimed), standing for Σ'_0.
In (257) the superscript is Σ (with a stray mark), and 'déf' is written 'dif'.
The final crossed-out symbol after V*_{Θ,X} is a scribbled-over subscript, not meaningful text.
